understanding: The supplied code describes a Raft library with separate protocol, replication, FSM and snapshot responsibilities. Recovered behavior is partial: client admission, voter-index aggregation, FSM dispatch helpers, snapshot capture, snapshot installation and file-sink finalization are visible. Replication evidence producers, leader commitment consumption, election helpers, startup reconstruction and concrete adapter selection remain unread. Documented guarantees are distinguished from observed guards and callback completion. No implementation correctness or defect is established.

target_profile.system_boundary: The github.com/hashicorp/raft library, including its protocol orchestration and available repository-owned adapters. Application FSM implementations and separately maintained storage backends are outside the supplied implementation evidence; built-in adapters remain within the discovery frontier.
protocol_contexts: Raft terms, server identities, voter membership and indexed typed log entries.
Candidate elections with optional pre-vote and a leadership-transfer bypass.
Asynchronous FSM application, snapshot capture and snapshot restore.
Versioned protocol messages, membership encoding and snapshot encoding.
external_interfaces: Apply, ApplyLog, Barrier and VerifyLeader return futures.
Transport supplies RPC delivery, pipelining, snapshot streaming and optional heartbeat fast-pass handling.
WithPreVote optionally supplies pre-vote RPC support.
FSM, BatchingFSM and FSMSnapshot supply application callbacks.
Log storage and snapshot storage are accessed through r.logs and r.snapshots; complete interface definitions remain unread.
Observer channels carry selected events; delivery implementation remains unread.
ownership: runCandidate processes candidate-state events in the main protocol loop.
commitment serializes voter-index and commit-index access with a mutex.
runFSM owns local application progress variables and callback helpers.
takeSnapshot requests FSM capture and separately requests configuration state owned by the main thread.
installSnapshot coordinates snapshot storage, an asynchronous FSM restore request and protocol metadata updates.
FileSnapshotSink implements repository-owned file finalization and publication.
selection_injection: runFSM selects BatchingFSM and ConfigurationStore behavior through interface assertions on r.fsm.
installSnapshot selects full old-log removal when r.logs implements MonotonicLogStore and reports IsMonotonic; otherwise it selects compaction.
Transport permits implementations to ignore SetHeartbeatHandler and deliver heartbeats through Consumer instead.
Constructor wiring, available storage implementations and active transport/storage variants require source acquisition.
variants: Pre-vote enabled versus disabled; leadership transfer bypasses pre-vote.
Optional ConfigurationStore in the single-entry path.
Legacy peer-list versus explicit configuration snapshot metadata.
Monotonic log-store cleanup versus trailing-log compaction.
File snapshot synchronization depends on noSync and operating system.
Protocol-version-dependent membership encoding is documented; active version is unknown.
unknowns: NewRaft initialization, goroutine startup, adapter ownership and recovery selection are unread.
The supplied capability probe establishes offline compilation availability only.
No actual application, deployment configuration or concrete failure contract is supplied.
Precise asynchronous or crash schedule control is unavailable unless a later experiment establishes it.

activities.purpose: Form and advance log decisions using reported replica progress.
activities.realization_summary: commitment records increasing voter match indices and advances its local commit index through an order statistic and startIndex threshold. The actual disk-write and replication-response producers, and the leader's downstream consumption, remain unresolved.
variants: Voter set can be replaced by setConfiguration.
unknowns: Persistence meaning of each match caller.
Leader dispatch, follower acceptance and commit-index consumption.

activities.purpose: Acquire and change protocol authority and term context.
activities.realization_summary: runCandidate selects pre-vote or election, tallies results, requests follower transitions on higher terms and leader transition on enough granted votes. Helper implementations and result provenance are unread. Snapshot installation also changes role and term when the request term is higher.
variants: Leadership-transfer election privilege reset on candidate-loop exit.

activities.purpose: Restore replicas from retained snapshots and resume participation.
activities.realization_summary: installSnapshot stores the incoming stream, waits for a restore future, updates snapshot/application/configuration metadata and attempts log cleanup. Startup recovery and incremental replication after installation are not yet recovered.
unknowns: Restart snapshot selection and log replay.

activities.realization_summary: The implementation distinguishes latest and committed configurations and their log indices. commitment.setConfiguration replaces its voter map. Snapshot creation consumes committed configuration metadata, while installation sets both latest and committed metadata.
unknowns: Configuration proposal, admission, activation and rollback call sites.
Enforcement of the documented one-uncommitted-configuration restriction.

activities.purpose: Dispatch selected log entries to the application and track callback progress.
activities.realization_summary: runFSM implements separate single-entry and batching helpers, response correlation, snapshot capture and restore helpers. Application callback bodies are supplied by clients; library filtering and scheduling remain inside the boundary.
unknowns: Queue dispatch and shutdown tail of runFSM.
Provenance and ordering of commitTuple inputs.
Application callback semantics in a selected deployment.

activities.purpose: Publish recovery representations and reclaim retained history.
activities.realization_summary: takeSnapshot captures FSM metadata, obtains committed configuration metadata, persists and closes a sink, updates last-snapshot metadata and compacts logs. FileSnapshotSink.Close implements finalization, metadata writing, rename, conditional directory synchronization and reaping. Ordinary log persistence is still a frontier.
unknowns: Metadata writing, listing, opening and reaping implementations.

activities.purpose: Admit client operations and communicate operation outcomes.
activities.realization_summary: ApplyLog and Barrier return futures after channel handoff or immediate enqueue/shutdown errors. Application helpers populate responses after callback processing. Apply documentation explicitly preserves outcome ambiguity on leadership loss and describes restore-aborted writes.

facts.meaning: The specific initialized future was sent on applyCh. This establishes handoff, not leadership, persistence, commitment or application.

facts.meaning: At an advancement event, the commitment object assigned an index greater than its previous commitIndex and at least startIndex, based on a majority order statistic of its then-current recorded voter indices. Actual persistence of those reports is not independently established here.

facts.validity_context: Historical assertion about a recalculate advancement under the mutex; it does not assert that a later replacement voter set supports the same index.

facts.meaning: For a selected command, the application callback returned and the corresponding optional future was populated and responded to with nil error by the helper. This does not independently establish upstream commitment or application durability.

identity.value: Log index, term and command object supplied to the helper

facts.validity_context: Normal completion of the command branch in applySingle, or a normally returning ApplyBatch with the checked response count.
facts.durability: Callback-dependent effects; completion representation is volatile.

facts.meaning: FSM.Snapshot returned a handle without error, paired by the helper with its current local lastIndex and lastTerm. The handle has not thereby been persisted.
facts.validity_context: Successful nonzero-index snapshot-helper completion; content fidelity depends on the application callback contract.
facts.durability: Application-owned capture handle until Release; not a stored recovery artifact.
unknowns: Release invalidates further handle use but does not erase the historical capture-return event.

facts.meaning: For this takeSnapshot invocation, Persist and Close returned nil, last-snapshot metadata was updated and compaction returned nil before the snapshot ID was returned. This is an orchestration result whose recovery meaning depends on the selected adapters.
facts.durability: Storage-adapter-dependent; successful callback returns alone do not establish crash durability.
facts.recovery: Snapshot Open and startup selection remain unread.

facts.meaning: The handler obtained successful sink-close and restore-future results, updated snapshot/application/configuration metadata, attempted cleanup and set Success true. Cleanup success is not part of this assertion.
facts.validity_context: Successful terminal handler branch; response delivery happens through deferred Respond.
facts.durability: Mixed adapter effects and local metadata; restart semantics unresolved.
facts.recovery: Not established by this handler alone.

facts.meaning: A Close call that entered with closed false completed finalize, writeMeta, rename, required parent-directory synchronization and ReapSnapshots without error.
facts.validity_context: Fresh-call successful branch only; excludes the already-closed early return.
facts.durability: Conditional synchronization is observed; full crash-recovery meaning requires metadata-writing and filesystem assumptions.
facts.recovery: Listing, Open and startup consumers remain unread.
unknowns: Whether a particular orchestration path selected this sink.
Consumers cannot infer this fresh-call fact from every nil Close return without additional context.
